name: USB-C (USB Type-C)
description: The reversible 24-pin USB connector. The A and B rows are point-symmetric (A1 sits opposite B12, etc.), which is what lets the plug go in either way up. USB 2.0 rides on the D+/D- pins (A6/A7, mirrored on B6/B7); the SuperSpeed TX/RX pairs carry USB 3.x, DisplayPort, or Thunderbolt alt modes; CC1/CC2 negotiate orientation, host/device role, and Power Delivery.

contacts.name: VBUS
contacts.description: bus power (5 V default, up to 20 V+ / 48 V with PD)

contacts.name: CC1
contacts.description: Configuration Channel: orientation, role, and PD negotiation (or VCONN)

contacts.name: D+
contacts.description: USB 2.0 data + (mirrored on B6, joined in the cable)

contacts.name: SBU1
contacts.description: Sideband Use (alt-mode aux, e.g. DisplayPort AUX)

contacts.name: CC2
contacts.description: Configuration Channel 2 (the other orientation's CC, or VCONN)

variants: Reversibility: the receptacle is point-symmetric (A row vs B row mirrored), so the same signals are reachable in either plug orientation; the host uses whichever CC pin (CC1/CC2) is pulled to figure out which way up it went in.
A USB 2.0-only Type-C cable populates only VBUS, GND, D+/D-, and CC/VCONN -- the SuperSpeed pins are absent. Charge-only cables may omit even the data pins.
gotchas: CC1/CC2 are the brains: they detect orientation, decide host vs device (DFP/UFP), advertise current capability (Rp/Rd resistors), and carry the Power Delivery messages. A cable with the wrong/missing CC resistors won't enumerate or charge.
VBUS is 5 V by default but Power Delivery can negotiate up to 20 V (100 W) or 48 V (240 W with EPR). Never assume 5 V on a PD link; measure or you smoke something.
USB 2.0 D+/D- appear on BOTH A6/A7 and B6/B7 but are the same pair (bridged in the cable) -- there is only one USB 2.0 channel regardless of orientation.
The SuperSpeed pairs double as DisplayPort / Thunderbolt / other alt-mode lanes once negotiated over CC; the pin is physical, the protocol on it is not fixed.
notes: 24-pin receptacle pinout (A1-A12, B1-B12) cross-checked against the USB Type-C spec / Wikipedia. Physical row order shown logically A1..A12 / B1..B12; the connector is point-symmetric for reversibility (see variants).
